rubrics.criterion: Single-registration presentation is owned by the per-binding wiring record: the behavior that produces one registration's formatted row (indentation, scope/type/name/activation/deactivation/tag fragments and the exact separators) and the behavior that produces the registration's explanatory legend text both live on the record class itself, and the diagnostic reporting helpers no longer read the record's fields to assemble those strings. Method names, signatures, and how much thin delegation remains in the helpers may differ.
rubrics.rationale: The report helpers in this instance hold no state and mine the digest's fields to build their strings; the row and legend are the clearest record-knowledge held elsewhere, and the pinned report/legend tests must keep passing through the record-owned implementation.

rubrics.criterion: Snapshot-level report assembly is owned by the snapshot record: the full text report (container-label header line, default-scope line, one rendered line per recorded registration, and the registered-services count) is produced by behavior on the snapshot class, with the reporting helper at most delegating.
rubrics.rationale: The snapshot contains every input of the rendered report, so assembling the report is snapshot knowledge; the helper adds nothing but the call. The exact report text is pinned by the diagnostics tests and must survive.

rubrics.criterion: Per-registration classification semantics are owned by the wiring record: the grouping key built from a registration's scope and binding type (including the lifecycle suffix derived from activation/deactivation handler presence) and the statefulness classification (singleton scope, constant-value binding, or lifecycle handler presence) come from record-owned behavior, while counting and grouping across a collection may remain on the collection owner.
rubrics.rationale: Both statistics methods in this case reach the record only through loop bindings and derive every classification fact from digest fields; the key vocabulary and the statefulness definition are digest knowledge that the statistics class currently reproduces field by field.

rubrics.criterion: Comparison knowledge is split along its two data sources: the field-by-field description of how one recorded registration differs from a previously recorded one (the before -> after fragments for scope, binding type, name, tag count, and activation, in that precedence, or no difference) is owned by the wiring record class, and the identification of added and changed registrations across a baseline and a current snapshot is owned by the snapshot record class; the comparison helper no longer contains either field-by-field digest comparison logic or the per-registration added/changed reasoning.
rubrics.rationale: The comparator currently implements both a two-digest comparison and a two-snapshot walk while holding no state; each rule belongs with the data that solely defines it, and the difference objects (kinds, descriptions, ordering) are pinned by tests.

rubrics.criterion: Serialization field knowledge is owned by the records: which fields each recorded registration serializes into its JSON record (and under which keys and order) is assembled by the wiring record, and the snapshot serializes its own label, default scope, and digest collection into the payload; the codec layer performs only JSON text conversion, payload structural validation, and record reconstruction, without copying record field by record field.
rubrics.rationale: The codec currently copies seven digest fields and the snapshot header fields itself; the JSON inventory of a record is knowledge about that record, and the round-trip plus payload-rejection tests must keep passing unchanged.

rubrics.criterion: The runtime-status vocabulary for one registration is owned by the wiring record: the scope/binding-type placement fragment and the activation/deactivation wording used in the bound/unbound status sentence come from record-owned behavior, while the audit helper keeps the live-container consult and contributes at most the bound/unbound fact and final assembly; the record does not consult the container itself.
rubrics.rationale: The audit method in this case reads six digest fields to narrate status while using the container only for one isBound answer; the sentence's wording is digest knowledge mixed into the audit path, and dragging the live container dependency into the data record would be the wrong direction.

rubrics.criterion: The same relocation is extended to the remaining register-mining path even though it is less data-hungry: the qualifier semantics of one registration (its tag names, its name-based qualifier, and the unqualified fallback when neither is present) is owned by the wiring record, with only usage counting across the collection remaining elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: The qualifier usage tally in this instance mines the digest's tag and name fields per registration as well; a repair that stops at the most data-hungry locations leaves the same maintenance shape behind, though this location's narrower slice makes it less central.

rubrics.criterion: The public surface survives the reorganization: every subsystem symbol exported from the package root before the change — both wiring record classes, all diagnostic operator classes, the descriptor contracts of the records, the line-writer port and its string implementation, and the serialization payload and comparison result types — still resolves from the package's entry point, and the interchange/status contract types remain importable from their previous public paths (in place or via re-export).
rubrics.rationale: The diagnostics subsystem is re-exported for downstream packages and the pinned tests construct these types through the public exports; relocation must not silently narrow the package's entry-point surface or strand type-only contracts.

rubrics.criterion: No stale duplicated implementations of the relocated knowledge remain in the production sources: the registration row and legend formatting, the grouping key and statefulness classification, the registration-change comparison fragments, the per-registration JSON record assembly, and the status vocabulary each exist exactly once (on the record classes), with no leftover copies still wired into any diagnostic operator.
rubrics.rationale: In this case the relocated knowledge is exactly the string and key vocabulary previously implemented in the operators; a repair that clones rather than moves would leave the maintenance burden doubled instead of removed.

rubrics.criterion: The relocation leaves no dead debris in the production sources: no unused imports, no unused private members or parameters, and no commented-out or unreferenced leftovers of the moved logic remain in the diagnostic operators or the record modules.
rubrics.rationale: This instance moves string-assembly and classification logic wholesale out of five operator classes; mechanical cut-and-paste relocation characteristically leaves unused imports and parameters behind in exactly those files.

rubrics.criterion: The line-streaming boundary still behaves as a port: streaming the recorded identifiers still performs one writeLine call per registration, in snapshot order, on the passed-in line-writer (not a single batched call, a returned string, or a dependency on the string implementation), so any custom sink implementation keeps observing lines one by one.
rubrics.rationale: The writer port is the subsystem's one integration boundary and its per-line semantics are what a logging or terminal consumer would rely on; the pinned test only checks the accumulated string, so batching would pass tests while regressing real sinks.

rubrics.criterion: The serialized snapshot form is byte-stable across the reorganization: serializing the same recorded snapshot produces byte-identical JSON (same key set, same key order) as before, so snapshot files produced by the earlier arrangement still round-trip and text-compare equal, and non-payload text is still rejected by the parse guard.
rubrics.rationale: Serialization formats outlive refactors in real maintenance flows and the round-trip test alone does not pin key order; this instance's payloads are alphabetically keyed and must stay so.

rubrics.criterion: The wiring records gain no live-runtime dependency: neither record class imports or references the container package or holds a container reference, and no record-owned behavior takes the live container as an input; recorded-state knowledge remains independent of the runtime, with the audit helper remaining the only place the container is consulted.
rubrics.rationale: The audit method is the only live-container consumer in this instance, and relocation is the natural moment to accidentally push the container dependency into the otherwise package-agnostic record data types, inverting the intended dependency direction.
